title: Inline SVG images need a text label
summary: An <svg> with role="img" has no accessible text, so screen readers cannot describe it. Add an aria-label or a <title> inside the SVG.
problem: An inline <svg> element has role="img" but contains no <title> and has no aria-label or aria-labeledby. Assistive technology treats it as an image with no name, so the drawing is either skipped or announced with no description.
whoItAffects: Screen reader users cannot tell what a logo, icon or chart drawn with SVG represents. When the SVG is the only content of a link or button, that control has no name at all.
steps: Find inline <svg> elements that have role="img". The scan result shows the exact markup.
If the graphic carries meaning, add aria-label with a short description, or add a <title> as the first child of the SVG.
If it is decoration beside visible text, remove role="img" and add aria-hidden="true" so it is skipped.
For a complex chart, keep the label short and put the full data in a nearby table or paragraph.
before:
<svg role="img" width="48" height="48" viewBox="0 0 48 48">
  <circle cx="24" cy="24" r="20" fill="#0b5cad"/>
</svg>
after:
<svg role="img" aria-label="Fernwood Garden Supply logo" width="48" height="48" viewBox="0 0 48 48">
  <circle cx="24" cy="24" r="20" fill="#0b5cad"/>
</svg>
whyItMatters: Graphics that carry meaning need a text alternative under WCAG 1.1.1, a Level A criterion. A logo or chart with no name hides its message from anyone who cannot see it.
howToCheck: Open the browser accessibility inspector, select the <svg> and read its Name. An empty Name means the label is missing. A screen reader should read your description.
